policy_notes.note: HUD 2026 Budget Management Letter: vouchers are funding-constrained. PHAs asked to stop issuing new vouchers (except HUD-VASH and FYI), pause new project-based voucher commitments, and cut payment standards, ending exception payment standards and staying inside the 90-110% basic range. Expect payment standards toward the low end of the range.
NSPIRE inspections for vouchers delayed to 2027-02-01 (third extension). Until then PHAs may still inspect under the old HQS (24 CFR 982.401). The checklist here aims at both.

Emergency Housing Vouchers are ending: families under EHV HAP contracts on 2026-09-30 move to Tenant Protection Vouchers by 2026-12-31 (PIH 2026-25); closeout from early 2027. For a landlord the lease continues as an ordinary voucher.
PHAs may use HCV admin fees for landlord signing/retention bonuses, security and utility deposits and holding fees (PIH 2022-18). Optional and per PHA; 2026 budget pressure makes them scarcer.

reasons: City STR ordinance is enjoined / in court: 2023 STR registration (Ch. 42B) and zoning ordinances are under a temporary injunction entered Dec 6, 2023; the city says it cannot enforce them meanwhile.

Allowed only in some zoning districts: 2023 zoning amendment allows 'short-term rental lodging' by right only in MO(A), GO(A), multifamily, central area, mixed use, multiple commercial and urban corridor districts (no single-family), but enforcement is enjoined.
Caps/density: Zoning text limits one STR per rentable unit; no other cap in force while the injunction stands.

Pending: City of Dallas v. Dallas Short-Term Rental Alliance, No. 25-0748: petition granted Oct 23, 2026; oral argument reset to Jan 14, 2027. Court of appeals (05-23-01309-CV, Jul 18, 2025) affirmed in part, reversed in part.

permit.value: 2023 STR registration (Ch. 42B) and zoning ordinances are under a temporary injunction entered Dec 6, 2023; the city says it cannot enforce them meanwhile.

primary_residence.value: No owner-occupancy rule in force (2023 ordinances enjoined).

zones.value: 2023 zoning amendment allows 'short-term rental lodging' by right only in MO(A), GO(A), multifamily, central area, mixed use, multiple commercial and urban corridor districts (no single-family), but enforcement is enjoined.

caps.value: Zoning text limits one STR per rentable unit; no other cap in force while the injunction stands.

max_occupancy.value: Codified Ch. 42B (enjoined, not enforced while the injunction stands): max three people per bedroom and 12 in total, two-night minimum stay, guest cars limited to off-street spaces.

taxes.value: Owner must collect the 9% city hotel occupancy tax and remit monthly; the city has no platform collection agreement. State HOT of 6% (Tax Code 156.052) also applies.

listing_id.value: Ch. 42B (enjoined) requires every listing or ad to show the Dallas STR registration number plus occupancy, sound, vehicle and parking limits and the two-night minimum; platforms may not take fees for unregistered STRs.

pending.value: City of Dallas v. Dallas Short-Term Rental Alliance, No. 25-0748: petition granted Oct 23, 2026; oral argument reset to Jan 14, 2027. Court of appeals (05-23-01309-CV, Jul 18, 2025) affirmed in part, reversed in part.

state_preemption.value: No state STR preemption statute found. Zaatari v. City of Austin (Tex. App.-Austin, Nov 27, 2019, No. 03-17-00812-CV) partly struck Austin's STR rules; review denied Jun 11, 2021. Dallas STR zoning ban is before the Texas Supreme Court (No. 25-0748).
